chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Yahya al-Azraq said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is killed and leaves a debt, but has no property, so his heirs take the blood money (diyah); is it upon them to pay his debt? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And if he left nothing?' He said, 'Yes, they only took his blood money, so it is upon them to pay his debt.'

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood money or compensation paid for killing or injuring someone
key_terms.يَقْضُوا: To pay off or settle (a debt)

ai.seo_question: How are a deceased person's debts paid if they have no other assets but receive blood money?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that blood money (diyah) is treated as part of the deceased's estate, ensuring creditors are paid even if no other assets remain. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that diyah is not merely a gift to heirs but a financial asset subject to the same obligations as the deceased's property, prioritizing debt settlement before inheritance distribution.
